candidate.educational_objective: Perform hand hygiene before an aseptic invasive-device task regardless of planned glove use.

options.A: Before the aseptic task, even though gloves will be worn
options.B: Only after the procedure if gloves remain intact
options.C: Only when the hands are visibly soiled
options.D: Hand hygiene is unnecessary when sterile gloves are used

candidate.rationale: CDC recommends hand hygiene before performing an aseptic task such as placing an indwelling device. CDC also states that gloves are not a substitute for hand hygiene.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Hand hygiene is required before aseptic tasks, and gloves do not replace hand hygiene.
candidate.source_document_title: Clinical Safety: Hand Hygiene for Healthcare Workers
candidate.source_locator: Recommendations > Know when to clean your hands; Know when to wear gloves
candidate.stem: A nurse is preparing to insert an indwelling urinary catheter. When should hand hygiene be performed?
